column7: 2026-11-04: parseBytes: only plain numbers + binary units (KiB..YiB), case-sensitive. kB/MB/GB deliberately unsupported (throw) until storage team says how to read them (1000 vs 1024).

2026-11-04: Storage team decision: on this branch, units without the 'i' (KB/kB, MB, GB...) read as powers of 1024 (1 KB = 1024, 1 MB = 1048576) because users paste sizes from Windows Explorer. Not implemented yet; planned for next session. Currently they throw.

2026-11-04: billing-svc: parseBytes() (plain numbers + KiB..YiB, case-sensitive; kB/MB/GB throw) is already committed in dfcc822 with tests and types; verified npm test passes. Billing service pins this branch, so keep decimal units unsupported here until the storage team decides 1000 vs 1024 (see storage-app log).

2026-11-04: billing-svc: when decimal units are added on this branch, they are strict SI: 1 kB = 1000, 1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes, matching prettyBytes output. Reason: billing quotes in strict SI. Deliberately differs from storage-app's plan to read KB/MB as 1024; do not merge that reading here.
2026-11-04: parseBytes: implemented kB/KB/MB..YB as powers of 1024 (case-sensitive; only kB and KB for kilo; bit units still throw). Documented in readme + index.d.ts. Not committed yet.
